title: SCHOOLED: Is State Leadership at Odds with Teacher Buy-In?
author: Mike Petrilli
summary: This SCHOOLED roundup opens a debate on whether states can mandate High-Quality Instructional Materials (HQIM) without disempowering educators. Kalman Hettleman argues for state leadership, citing Maryland's attempt to replicate the Mississippi Miracle under Carey Wright. Robert Pondiscio offers a franchise analogy—states set standards but localities retain day-to-day operational autonomy. Peter Greene pushes back sharply: state capitals are better at politics than pedagogy, and HQIM mandates distort through a game of telephone at every implementation level, as Common Core demonstrated. The roundup also covers neuroscientist Jared Cooney Horvath's evidence that PISA scores are 66 points lower for students using computers 6+ hours daily, with the Flynn Effect now reversed among the youngest generation; Chad Aldeman counters that the causal link to technology is unproven because declines preceded the digital inflection point in several states. Additional threads include Democrats' retreat from education reform (Elorza/Austin), AI-enabled assessment innovation (Swift), Shaka Mitchell's O'Toole Executive Compass framework for policy durability, and Ohio/Texas research showing industry credentials vary dramatically in wage outcomes by field, with manufacturing certifications outperforming education and arts credentials.
points: The HQIM state-vs-local debate centers on a false dichotomy: strong state curriculum standards and meaningful teacher buy-in are not mutually exclusive; Maryland's implementation attempt represents the first blue-state test of whether the 'both/and' approach can survive more entrenched local-control politics.

Horvath's PISA data shows students using computers 6+ hours daily score 66 points lower—roughly two-thirds of a standard deviation, equivalent to dropping from the 50th to the 24th percentile—and the Flynn Effect (each generation +6 IQ points) reversed in the last 15 years as digital technology permeated young people's lives.

Aldeman's counter-argument: test score declines in states like Alabama preceded the 'digital inflection' point, suggesting screen time is a hypothesis, not a proven cause; the evaporation of K-12 accountability is an equally plausible culprit that is harder to address politically.

Mitchell's O'Toole Executive Compass shows durable education policy must address all four values simultaneously—Liberty, Equality, Efficiency, and Community—and school choice advocates have learned to speak all four languages while most other reform movements have not.

Ohio and Texas research on industry credentials shows wages vary by up to 35% above or 30% below average depending on credential type; manufacturing credentials yield durable long-term returns; education, human services, and arts credentials often do not—states should count students as career-ready only when they complete coursework AND earn an aligned credential.
quotes: The debate over state control should avoid false dichotomies. It's not either/or. Key is how to impose state standards and gain buy-in by local districts and classroom teachers. This is a focus of the Maryland effort, and here's hoping it succeeds. (Hettleman)

The folks in state capitals are far better at politics than they are at education. That's how they got there. 'We talked to hundreds of actual teachers and realized we were headed in exactly the wrong direction, so we have changed our direction and emphasis,' said no state-level edu-bureaucrat ever. (Greene)

On the PISA scale, 66 points is a very large difference, roughly two-thirds of a standard deviation—equivalent to dropping from the 50th to the 24th percentile, or roughly two letter grades. This pattern holds across every country tested by PISA. (Horvath)
The screen time argument should be seen as a hypothesis, not a fact. (Aldeman)
The education solutions that actually gain traction are the ones with a tent big enough to make room for all four [values—Liberty, Equality, Efficiency, Community]. (Mitchell)
